title: GNU Make / Makefile analyzer (M60, 2026-09-27)
question: The website advertises a Make analyzer via SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES. Do we have one, and is it any good?
verdict: We had one: wired into engine.ts, advertised, and named by ZERO gates. It is now gated, measured and substantially rebuilt. 17 defects found and fixed; recall/precision 1.000000 against an independent oracle; completeness A-H 8/8.

sourceVsWasm.anonymousNote: 130 anonymous ids in the wasm vs 91 declared: node-types.json deduplicates identical anonymous tokens the id table lists once per id. Not part of the proof, and recorded rather than hidden.
sourceVsWasm.namedIdNote: 46 named IDS for 44 unique names (`word` and `text` each hold 2 ids) — which is why the inventory prints 46 against a 44-entry spec.

corpus.rule: filenames in {Makefile, makefile, GNUmakefile, Makefile.am, Makefile.in} or suffix .mk; skipping .git, node_modules, vendor, target, dist, build, .venv, deps

differential.independence: the oracle derives names by a THIRD route (node text + delimiters, regex for assignments) and is two-phase with a per-frame owner; of the 5 rounds it took to reach 1.0, FOUR were oracle bugs and ONE was a real analyzer defect (the ${VAR} form), which is the argument for running it.

dangleAdjudication.note: only the operator-polluted class (112 edge ends) was a real defect; the rest are structural to GNU Make and are what the `uses` class exists for. 0 fell into a true-dangler bucket.

ruled.why: GNU Make has no type declaration, no base clause and no inheritance among its 44 named node types. The kind is not merely unused, it is INEXPRESSIBLE: there is no syntax from which
Same measurement as `extends`: Make has no interface to implement. A target that happens to satisfy a convention is a convention, not a declared type relationship, and reading one
The one kind with a REAL construct, and the ruling is measured rather than assumed. `override VAR = value` (2 occurrences) means this definition wins over a command-line or environ
Make has no `new` and no object construction. A recipe is a shell command that produces files; it is not an expression that yields a value, and nothing in the tree resembles a cons

complexity.linearity: no growth in per-node cost with file size: consistent with linear
complexity.withdrawnClaim: the first version bucketed by QUARTILES and printed a 1.208 'spread' with n=1 and n=0 buckets. 50 of 99 files sit within a few nodes of each other, so quartiles cannot work here; a spread over an empty bucket is not a measurement.

headline: line_number absent on 0 of 1,784 relationships (a product field; the address surfaces serve call-site positions from it) -> now 5,445/5,445
55 symbols carried their assignment operator (CGO_ENABLED?), which broke 112 edge ends BY CONSTRUCTION
references collected only from variable_assignment and rule, so a bare top-level $(foreach ... $(eval $(call ...))) produced zero edges
substitution_reference never read (a SIBLING of variable_reference, not a child) -> 9 corpus references lost
bare `export NAME` invisible (wraps a list, no assignment node anywhere)
computed includes dropped (`include $(shell ...)` is a shell_function node, not a function_call)
exports hardcoded [] -> a makefile's public surface unanswerable
imports sourced at a literal "makefile" -> two files including the same path produced the same edge
${VAR} (Make's second expansion form, 68 occurrences in 14 of 99 files) not normalised -> each fact published twice, one spelling dangling
define produced a constant, so a `calls` edge pointed at a value that cannot be called
sharedHarness: the F5 file picker required a dotted extension, and Make's files are named `Makefile` — so the lane read as EMPTY rather than unchecked. Added an additive opt-in `fileNames` list; no other lane's matching changes.

the F5 label allowlist registered only 3 of the 6 labels the make oracle derives, so 1,500 analyzer edges were filtered off and reported as 1,498 MISSING (92% of truth) while the analyzer was emitting 2,109 edges for those 53 files.

survivingMutantsFoundAndFixed: make/accept-keywords-as-names SURVIVED the first run: the fixtures had no forbid on the `export` keyword, so a mutant resurrecting 6 bad edges changed nothing. A surviving mutant is a hole in the suite, not a pass.

make/ignore-brace-expansion-form also survived: the fix normalises the target during EXTRACTION, so a result-level transform finds no ${...} to rewrite and the revert is a silent no-op. Rewritten to take the source and re-wrap only edges whose own line really contains the brace form.

gates.grammar pin: make registered; 0 drift; source<->wasm exact 0/0 both directions
gates.zero-unknown census: 0 unknown / 0 empty / 0 bad ranges / 0 ownerless / 0 symbol-free; 5,445/5,445 line_number
gates.doc-truth audit: 49 claims, 0 stale, self-test PASS — corrupting the "contains edges" l

gaps.summary: `VPATH = src` is a declared node type the analyzer does not model, so the search path is not recorded. 0 occurrences across all 99 corpus files, so there is no evidence to design against and no regres

`.RECIPEPREFIX = >` changes what a recipe line looks like, so ignoring it means recipe lines using a non-default prefix are not recognized as recipes. 0 occurrences in this corpus (every one of the 99

GRAMMAR limitation, not an analyzer defect, and deliberately NOT patched. The target-scoped form `target: export VAR = value` — 10 lines across 2 of 99 files (boundary/Makefile, tf-aws-components/.../

notClaimed: any absolute performance budget: the box ran at load 49-50 throughout with nine agents on it, so every timing here is relative with the load recorded
any weight behind `calls`: it rests on ONE corpus site, and the count says so

incidents: the hcl LANG_CONFIGS entry was NEVER COMMITTED — it lived only in a dirty worktree and a concurrent `git checkout` deleted it, after which `--lang hcl` threw `unknown language hcl`. Restored here and marked as a restoration; the gate itself then caught my reconstruction being wrong (I had required `calls`, which hcl rules N/A), so the restored entry is verified rather than assumed.

`script/**` is NOT in the typecheck program (root tsconfig includes `src/**/*.ts` only), so `npx tsc --noEmit` never sees the harnesses. I reported a shared file as type-clean on that basis while it had a syntax error. `bun build <file> --target=bun` is the real syntax gate for script/**.
`open(p,'wb')` truncates BEFORE the write fails: a full disk turned one mutant insertion into an empty mutate-analyzer.ts. All writes in this lane go temp-file + os.replace, verified after each.
